notice: RN bank batch 140: Maternity case studies: shoulder dystocia, uterine rupture, amniotic fluid embolism and precipitous birth. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings of shoulder dystocia.

rationale.correct: The turtle sign after the head delivers means shoulder dystocia.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each injury, indicate who is mainly at risk after shoulder dystocia.

rationale.correct: Both mother and newborn are at risk.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse should first {{b1}}, and must never {{b2}}.

options.text: call for help and assist with the McRoberts maneuver
push on the top of the uterus
pull hard on the head
leave to get equipment
apply fundal pressure
time the event
apply suprapubic pressure
help the client flex the thighs

rationale.correct: McRoberts with suprapubic pressure; never fundal pressure.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Place the steps in the usual order.

rationale.correct: Help, McRoberts, suprapubic pressure, internal maneuvers, newborn readiness.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: After the birth, which documentation actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Record the time the head and body delivered
List each maneuver in order and who did it
Record the newborn's arm movement at birth
Write that the provider was too slow
Leave the event out of the chart to avoid legal issues

rationale.correct: Objective, timed documentation.
references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings of uterine rupture.

rationale.correct: Sudden pain, FHR collapse, lost station and shock during TOLAC mean rupture.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each factor, indicate whether it raises the risk of uterine rupture.

rows.text: Birth less than 18 months after the cesarean
Previous low transverse incision with spontaneous labor
Misoprostol for ripening after a cesarean

rationale.correct: Scar type and uterotonics affect rupture risk.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse should {{b1}} and call for {{b2}}.

options.text: stop the oxytocin
increase the oxytocin
perform a vaginal exam to confirm
encourage pushing
an emergency cesarean and blood products
an epidural
a repeat ultrasound tomorrow
a chaplain only

rationale.correct: Stop oxytocin and prepare for surgery.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which actions should the nurse take while the operating room is prepared? Select all that apply.

options.text: Two large-bore IVs and rapid fluids
Type and crossmatch, massive transfusion protocol
Insert a urinary catheter if time allows
Neonatal team to the operating room
Wait for the FHR to recover before moving
Give terbutaline to relax the uterus

rationale.correct: Resuscitate, blood, catheter and newborn team.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse hands the client over to the operating room team. Which information is most important to include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Time of onset and FHR since then
Previous cesarean type and oxytocin dose
Current vital signs and fluids given
Allergies and blood type
The client's preferred birth playlist
A detailed history of the first pregnancy's prenatal visits

rationale.correct: A focused handoff in an emergency.
references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

questions.stem: After surgery, for each finding, indicate whether it shows recovery or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Hematuria with clots in the catheter
Newborn in NICU on cooling therapy
"Can I try a vaginal birth next time?"

rationale.correct: Recovery; bladder injury, newborn and future counseling need follow-up.

perOption.r5:c1: Future births need repeat cesarean before labor.
perOption.r5:c2: Future births need repeat cesarean before labor.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

questions.stem: For each phase, indicate the main problem in amniotic fluid embolism.

rows.text: Bleeding from IV sites and the uterus

rationale.correct: Collapse comes first, then DIC.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse should start CPR with {{b1}}, and if there is no return of circulation by 4 minutes, prepare for {{b2}}.

options.text: manual left uterine displacement
the client turned fully prone
the head of the bed raised
no changes from usual CPR
perimortem cesarean birth within 5 minutes of arrest
waiting 30 minutes
stopping CPR
vaginal birth

rationale.correct: Left uterine displacement and perimortem cesarean.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Circulation returns after the cesarean, and the client starts to bleed from IV sites. Which orders should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Massive transfusion with plasma, platelets and cryoprecipitate
Tranexamic acid
Uterotonics for atony
Fibrinogen, platelets and coagulation tests often
Heparin to treat clotting
Hold all blood products until labs return

rationale.correct: Balanced products, TXA, uterotonics and frequent labs.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The partner is in the waiting room asking what is happening. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Assign a staff member to stay with and update the partner
Use simple, honest language
Offer a chaplain or social worker
Tell the partner everything will be fine
Avoid speaking to the partner until the client is stable

rationale.correct: Honest, supported communication.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that show the transition phase moving to birth.

questions.stem: For each phase of the first stage, indicate its typical features.

rows.text: 6 to 7 cm, focused, more intense contractions
8 to 10 cm, irritable, nausea, shaking, urge to push
Contractions every 2 to 3 minutes, 60 to 90 seconds, strong

rationale.correct: Phases differ in dilation and behavior.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse should {{b1}}, and support the head with {{b2}}.

options.text: stay with the client and prepare for birth
leave to find the provider
hold the client's legs together
tell the client to stop pushing completely
gentle pressure to prevent a sudden expulsion
firm traction on the head
no support
pushing the head back in

rationale.correct: Stay and control the birth.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: After the head delivers, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Feel for a cord around the neck
Slip a loose cord over the head
Let the shoulders deliver with the next contraction, guiding gently
Dry the newborn and place skin to skin
Cut the cord immediately before the shoulders deliver
Pull on the cord to deliver the placenta quickly

rationale.correct: Check for a cord, guide the shoulders, warm the newborn.

perOption.e: Only if tight and cannot be reduced.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Birth
exhibits.body: Loose cord around the neck once.

questions.stem: After the birth, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Record the time of birth and who was present
Check the fundus and watch for bleeding
Do not pull on the cord; wait for signs of placental separation
Report the event to the provider on arrival
Document that the provider was late as the cause of any injury
Leave the client alone to call the family

rationale.correct: Document, assess bleeding and wait for the placenta.
references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Take action after a precipitous birth.

exhibits.title: 5 minutes
exhibits.body: Provider arrived. Placenta not yet delivered.

questions.stem: At 1 hour, for each finding, indicate whether it is expected or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Newborn temperature 36.6 C skin to skin
Severe perineal pain with a tense purple swelling

rationale.correct: A tense painful swelling after a rapid birth is a hematoma.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

caseStudies.title: Shoulder dystocia with a macrosomic baby

exhibits.title: Second stage
exhibits.body: A 32-year-old client with gestational diabetes on insulin is pushing at 40 weeks. Estimated fetal weight is 4,600 g. The second stage has lasted 2.5 hours.

rows.label: Head
cells: Delivered, then pulled back against the perineum (turtle sign)

rows.label: Next contraction
cells: No further progress with gentle traction

caseStudies.title: Uterine rupture during a trial of labor after cesarean

exhibits.title: Trial of labor after cesarean
exhibits.body: A 30-year-old client with one previous low transverse cesarean is in labor at 7 cm with oxytocin augmentation. The client suddenly screams with tearing abdominal pain between contractions.

rows.label: Abdomen
cells: Fetal parts easily felt under the skin

caseStudies.title: Amniotic fluid embolism with cardiac arrest

exhibits.title: Labor and delivery
exhibits.body: A 38-year-old client at 39 weeks had artificial rupture of membranes 5 minutes ago. The client suddenly says, "Something is wrong, I can't breathe," and becomes agitated.

caseStudies.title: Precipitous birth with the nurse alone

exhibits.title: Labor room
exhibits.body: A 29-year-old client (G4 P3) arrived at 8 cm. The provider is 20 minutes away. The client was calm with breathing but is now irritable, nauseated and shaking, and says, "I can't do this anymore." Minutes later the client says, "The baby is coming," and the head is crowning.

rows.label: Help
cells: Call light pressed; another nurse coming

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
